Item.OQ-1_-__option_1__user__2026-09-24_: kept outputs in one flat machine-local directory next to the journal, declared in the registry's state_files, 14-day age retention (precedent JOB_MAX_AGE_DAYS=14). Retention is IN scope (NFR-6).

Item.OQ-2_-__option_1: empty exit-0 output is always a non-ok outcome; the caller regex is an optional stricter check.

Item.OQ-3_-__option_1: the new outcome is never penalised.

Item.OQ-4_-__option_3: structured capability key only (qwen38 has no web search); latency stays in the journal.

Item.text: classify() maps an attempt to unavailable or context_overflow on output text only when the exit code is non-zero; an exit-0 attempt is never reclassified by words in the model's answer.

Regression test - a model that exits 0 and whose answer contains "quota" and "429" yields outcome ok, the answer reaches --out, no penalty is written; the existing non-zero-exit true-positive tests stay green.

The captured output of every attempt that actually ran and did not end ok (timeout, unavailable, error, runtime context_overflow, and the new check-failed outcome) is kept in a machine-local location instead of being deleted.
The journal line of an attempt carries the path of the kept output and its size in bytes; ok attempts and pre-flight context_overflow skips carry null.

The caller may pass an answer check (a regex that must match the output); an output that fails the check is a new non-ok outcome, the attempt is journalled as such, and the run continues to the next model of the role.
An attempt classified by the new outcome is not penalised (see OQ-3).
model-stats.py counts and renders the new outcome and tolerates journal lines with and without the new optional keys.
The registry records that qwen38 has no working web search as a structured capability; observed latency stays in the journal (read via model-stats.py), not in the registry (OQ-4 decision).
task-57 is re-run through model-run.sh --role executor; at least one executor model returns a card quoting a fetched 57.mskobr.ru page with its URL, and the journal line is recorded in the bd issue.
The header help text of model-run.sh (printed by --help) lists the new flag and the new outcome.

No new runtime dependency beyond what a stock Ubuntu has - bash, jq, GNU coreutils, grep, awk (already used) and GNU findutils (find, for retention) for the runner; Python 3 stdlib only for model-stats.py.

All 126 existing tests in `make test` stay green; new behaviour is covered by tests in test_model_run.py and test_model_stats.py using the synthetic-registry fixture (no real model, network or quota).
Kept outputs and the journal remain machine-local under the user's home directory, never committed, never cited by absolute path in committed documents.
The journal stays append-only, one line per attempt; schema changes are additive so existing lines still parse.
The journal line contains only facts (path, bytes, outcome) - never the output text itself, so no task or model content can leak through the journal.
Growth of kept outputs is bounded by an age-based retention rule.

Item.risk: Gating text patterns on non-zero exit hides a real outage whose wrapper exits 0.
Item.mitigation: The answer then reaches --out where the caller sees the error text; the caller check (FR-5) moves the run on without a wrong penalty; exit and outcome stay in the journal for a later sweep.

Item.risk: Kept outputs grow unbounded or hold task text the caller considers sensitive.
Item.mitigation: Machine-local only, age-based retention (NFR-6), never cited by absolute path.

Item.risk: A new outcome value is miscounted by an older reader.
Item.mitigation: model-stats.py is the only reader; updated and tested in the same change; its ok counting is unaffected.

Item.risk: A timed-out claude -p run leaves an empty kept file because the answer is buffered until the end.
Item.mitigation: The journal records the byte size (FR-4) so the reader knows before opening; tracing the 420 s cause stays LATER.

Item.risk: An over-strict caller regex turns every model into the new outcome and exhausts the role.
Item.mitigation: Exit 1 "exhausted" already exists (model-run.sh lines 184-185); every answer is kept (FR-3), so nothing is lost.

Item.risk: Refreshing glm-4.7 timing mixes two measurements (2k-token single prompt vs multi-turn web task).
Item.mitigation: OQ-4 - keep the two figures apart; only timeout_seconds matters at runtime.

Item.risk: The task-57 acceptance run depends on live pools and on 57.mskobr.ru being reachable for the chosen runner.
Item.mitigation: Acceptance asks for at least one executor model; the run is recorded evidence, never a pytest.

Feature.evidence_justification: Both defects cited from the Step 12 review of python-ai-skills-2fu and verified in this session (grep shows no reader of no_penalty_on besides a test; bash defers traps until a foreground child exits).

Item.text: model-run.sh penalises an attempt when its outcome is listed in the registry's policy.penalize_on (default ["unavailable"] when absent), or when the outcome is timeout and the model sets penalize_on_timeout.
The registry no longer carries policy.no_penalty_on (it is the complement of penalize_on and was read by nothing); the policy comment states that penalize_on is read by the runner.

On SIGINT or SIGTERM during an attempt, model-run.sh stops the running model command, writes one journal line with outcome interrupted and the kept output's path and size, and exits 130 (INT) or 143 (TERM) without waiting for the model timeout.
--help lists the interrupted outcome and the policy.penalize_on behaviour.
No new runtime dependency (bash, jq, coreutils).
make test stays green; each FR is proven by a test using the synthetic-registry fixture.

constraints.Item: Journal stays append-only and additive; interrupted is a new outcome value that model-stats.py renders generically.

scope_later.Item: Timeout diagnosis of glm-4.7 is python-ai-skills-v6z, not this feature.

Item.text: The registry has a role for web research whose models, in order, are glm-5.3-high, gpt-terra-high, sonnet-low.
A role may declare timeout_seconds; when present, model-run.sh uses it instead of each model's timeout_seconds for attempts made under that role; roles without it keep per-model timeouts.
The web-research role declares timeout_seconds 900.
Every model of the web-research role has capabilities.web_search true (checked by the shipped-registry test).
CLAUDE.md names the role and when to use it; --help mentions the role-level timeout.
No new runtime dependency; existing roles behave exactly as before (same timeouts).
make test green; FR-2 proven with the synthetic-registry fixture.
